items.title: Full Opus 5 vs Kimi K3 vs GPT-5.6 vs Claude Fable 5 comparison.
items.summary:
Full Opus 5 vs Kimi K3 vs GPT-5.6 vs Claude Fable 5 comparison.

Opus 5 just delivered a seriously impressive result in my 3D destruction physics benchmark.

I gave four frontier models the same challenge: build three self-contained HTML scenes with realistic physics.

The tasks:

🌪️ A tornado ripping through a field
🏗️ A wrecking ball demolishing an apartment block
🌉 An overloaded truck collapsing a truss bridge

Token usage / cost:
• Opus 5: 55.9K tokens — $1.40
• Fable 5: 55.1K tokens — $2.82
• Kimi K3: 35.7K tokens — $0.55
• GPT-5.6: 20.1K tokens — $0.31

Opus was the only model that convincingly completed all three scenarios.

The tornado actually lifted debris into the funnel, the wrecking ball fractured the building where it made contact, and the bridge failed in a way that sent the truck into the river.

The others struggled in different ways. Fable’s tornado had little to pick up, its building collapsed before impact, and the bridge disintegrated unrealistically. GPT-5.6 was the cheapest, but the wrecking ball never reached the building and the bridge failure lacked believable physics. Kimi K3 landed somewhere in between.

For complex browser-based physics simulations, Opus 5 is setting a very high bar.

items.title: EVERYONE IS TALKING ABOUT CLAUDE OPUS 5 BUILDING AAA GAMES. ALMOST NOBODY KNOWS WHY
items.summary:
EVERYONE IS TALKING ABOUT CLAUDE OPUS 5 BUILDING AAA GAMES. ALMOST NOBODY KNOWS WHY

Someone asked Claude Opus 5 to build a game inspired by For Honor x Rainbow Six.

Minutes later, it was already generating a playable 3D prototype

After comparing it with GPT-5.6 and other models, the creator called Opus 5 the best AI model for frontend and 3D development he's ever used.

But the real story isn't the game.

It's how Anthropic changed prompting.

Most people still write prompts as if they're talking to GPT-4-era models: long instructions, endless checklists, "verify your answer," "think step by step."

Opus 5 was built differently.

Anthropic's own guide says to stop micromanaging the model. Give it the goal, explain the context, remove unnecessary instructions, and let it reason on its own.

That's why you're suddenly seeing people build games, apps, and production-ready UIs instead of just getting better chat responses.

The biggest Opus 5 upgrade isn't higher benchmark scores.

It's that ai is starting to think like an engineer, not just respond like a chatbot

items.title: AI Labor Market Tracker: Jobs, Hiring and Adoption | Revelio Labs
items.summary:
The hiring process is producing fewer successful matches. The number of job postings required to one hire has been increasing for six years, while candidates increasingly report recruiter silence and poor communication. These trends predate ChatGPT, so they cannot be attributed entirely to generative AI. But AI may be making an existing problem worse by enabling candidates to submit more polished applications, weakening the signals employers use to identify strong candidates. [...] Exposure declining in postings

The decline does not prove that AI has already replaced this work. Employers may also be reacting to expectations about what AI will soon be able to do or to other changes in labor demand. But the pattern is consistent with some automation, or reduced reliance on highly exposed activities, already taking place.

For now, the clearest description may be: AI is automating work, but not jobs.

## How AI May Be Making Hiring Less Effective

AI is not only changing what employers hire people to do. It is also changing how candidates compete for jobs. [...] The first is AI exposure: the share of work activities performed in an occupation that current AI systems could plausibly do. Exposure does not mean that employers or workers in these roles are already using AI. The possibility alone can change behavior. Firms may decrease hiring in exposed roles, redirect demand toward different work, or reconsider which entry-level positions they need before they have fully deployed the technology. These are anticipatory effects: labor-market changes driven by what employers expect AI will be able to do, rather than by its observed use inside a company.

items.title: Employees at the world’s biggest AI companies are calling for a slowdown in AI development | CNN Business
items.summary:
The letter comes on the heels of major advancements and burgeoning threats from rapidly developing AI systems. OpenAI disclosed last week that two of its test models escaped a lab environment, bypassed its systems to gain access to the open internet and hacked a different company’s internal system.

“[T]here is a real risk that capability development rapidly accelerates beyond our ability to understand or control the resulting systems,” the signees said. “To realize AI’s potential, industry, government, and society at large may need the option to buy time to address emerging risks, develop security measures, and strengthen oversight.” [...] OpenAI said in a statement to CNN they agree with potentially pacing the development of AI, adding they “hope to contribute to work led by the U.S. government, alongside other labs” on the topic.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman suggested it may be time to slow down AI development in a podcast interview Tuesday. The OpenAI models that broke out of their test environment are fueling “long term questions” about how AI companies should address this new rate of progress.

“[W]e may have to pace the rate of AI development to give ourselves enough time for society to harden around these new capability levels,” Altman said.

Anthropic said in a statement they are “glad to see broad agreement” on the need to potentially slow AI development “so society can prepare.” [...] See all topics

Email 

Link Copied!

Top staffers from the biggest AI and technology companies urged the US government to slow the pace of artificial intelligence development so that safety and security measures can catch up in an open letter.

The US government should support an international effort to develop tools that can “deliberately pace the frontier of automated AI development,” according to the letter.

results.input: Giải giúp mình bài toán tích phân: nguyên hàm của x^2 là gì?

result.actual_text:
Nguyên hàm của $x^2$ là:

$$\int x^2 \, dx = \frac{x^3}{3} + C$$

Trong đó $C$ là hằng số tích phân.

**Giải thích:** Áp dụng công thức nguyên hàm tổng quát $\int x^n \, dx = \frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1} + C$ với $n = 2$, ta có:

$$\int x^2 \, dx = \frac{x^{2+1}}{2+1} + C = \frac{x^3}{3} + C$$

Nếu bạn cần tính **tích phân xác định** (có cận), cứ cung cấp cận trên và cận dưới, mình giải thêm cho!

results.input: Bạn là gì và làm được những gì?

result.actual_text:
Mình là một **Research Assistant** (trợ lý nghiên cứu) có quyền truy cập nhiều công cụ để hỗ trợ bạn tìm kiếm và xử lý thông tin. Dưới đây là tổng quan về mình:

---

### 🔍 Mình có thể làm gì:

**Tìm kiếm & Truy xuất thông tin:**
- **Tìm trên web** (`lookup`) — tra cứu tin tức, thông tin tổng quát khi chưa có URL cụ thể.
- **Tìm trên mạng xã hội** (`social_search`) — tìm kiếm bài đăng, tweet theo chủ đề.
- **Lấy bài đăng của một người cụ thể** (`timeline`) — xem timeline của ai đó trên X/Twitter (ví dụ: Sam Altman, Elon Musk, Andrej Karpathy, Yann LeCun...).
- **Lấy nội dung từ URL** (`fetch`) — đọc nội dung từ một link cụ thể.
- **Tìm trên Reddit** (`reddit_search`) — tìm thảo luận trên các subreddit.
- **Tìm repository GitHub** (`github_search`) — tìm mã nguồn mở.
- **Đọc file trong GitHub** (`github_file`) — đọc nội dung file/thư mục trong repo.

**Nghiên cứu học thuật:**
- **Tìm bài báo khoa học** (`papers`) — tìm trên arXiv.
- **Đọc nội dung bài báo** (`paper_text`) — trích xuất text từ bài báo arXiv.
- **Tìm bài báo đa lĩnh vực** (`semantic_scholar`) — tìm kiếm học thuật rộng hơn.
- **Tìm trên Stack Overflow** (`stackoverflow`) — tra cứu câu hỏi kỹ thuật.

**Xử lý & Trình bày dữ liệu:**
- **Đọc PDF** (`pdf_read`) — trích xuất text từ file PDF có URL.
- **Định dạng dữ liệu** (`format`) — trình bày kết quả thành văn bản theo nhiều định dạng (tóm tắt, dạng mục, thread...).

**Giao tiếp:**
- **Gửi tin nhắn** (`send`) — gửi nội dung đi (khi được xác nhận).
- **Xác nhận hành động** (`clarify`) — hỏi lại khi thiếu thông tin hoặc xác nhận trước khi gửi/post nội dung ra ngoài.

---

### 📌 Một số quy tắc mình tuân thủ:
- Nếu bạn yêu cầu **gửi/đăng/post** nội dung → mình sẽ hỏi xác nhận trước (`yes_no`).
- Nếu bạn yêu cầu lấy bài của **một người cụ thể** → mình cần biết handle/tên của họ.
- Nếu bạn nói **"bài này, link này"** mà không kèm URL → mình sẽ hỏi URL.
- Mình luôn truyền đúng **số lượng** (`limit`), **thời gian** (`timeframe`), và **từ khóa** (`query`) theo yêu cầu của bạn.

items.title: From Code to Care: How UC San Diego Is Leading the Way in AI for Health Care
items.summary:
One example is the use of AI-powered patient messaging to help people prepare for colonoscopies. By answering routine questions, sending personalized reminders and guiding patients through the often-complex preparation process, the technology reduced last-minute procedure cancellations from 10% to 3% while improving the patient experience. The result is better access to colorectal cancer screening and more time for care teams to focus on patients who need additional support. [...] Beyond patient messaging, AI is helping physicians prepare patients for procedures, streamline clinical documentation, improve communication and support complex medical decision making. The health system has also become a national testbed for responsible AI implementation, evaluating new technologies through rigorous clinical oversight before they are deployed in patient care.

“We’ve thought of three distinct categories of deployment for AI,” said Khalessi. “Patient-facing applications, clinical decision support tools and solutions that remove administrative burden to improve patient access and allow physicians to focus on care.” [...] Researchers across the university are developing AI tools that are transforming medicine long before patients arrive in the exam room. UC San Diego scientists have created deep-learning models that can predict life-threatening sepsis hours earlier than traditional methods, giving clinicians valuable time to begin treatment. Researchers have also developed AI technologies that improve radiation treatment planning for cervical cancer, making the process faster and more precise, while other teams are using AI to uncover new causes of diseases such as Alzheimer’s and identify potential therapeutic targets.

items.title: AI Labor Market Tracker: Jobs, Hiring and Adoption | Revelio Labs
items.summary:
The hiring process is producing fewer successful matches. The number of job postings required to one hire has been increasing for six years, while candidates increasingly report recruiter silence and poor communication. These trends predate ChatGPT, so they cannot be attributed entirely to generative AI. But AI may be making an existing problem worse by enabling candidates to submit more polished applications, weakening the signals employers use to identify strong candidates. [...] Exposure declining in postings

The decline does not prove that AI has already replaced this work. Employers may also be reacting to expectations about what AI will soon be able to do or to other changes in labor demand. But the pattern is consistent with some automation, or reduced reliance on highly exposed activities, already taking place.

For now, the clearest description may be: AI is automating work, but not jobs.

## How AI May Be Making Hiring Less Effective

AI is not only changing what employers hire people to do. It is also changing how candidates compete for jobs. [...] The first is AI exposure: the share of work activities performed in an occupation that current AI systems could plausibly do. Exposure does not mean that employers or workers in these roles are already using AI. The possibility alone can change behavior. Firms may decrease hiring in exposed roles, redirect demand toward different work, or reconsider which entry-level positions they need before they have fully deployed the technology. These are anticipatory effects: labor-market changes driven by what employers expect AI will be able to do, rather than by its observed use inside a company.

items.title: Employees at the world’s biggest AI companies are calling for a slowdown in AI development | CNN Business

The letter comes on the heels of major advancements and burgeoning threats from rapidly developing AI systems. OpenAI disclosed last week that two of its test models escaped a lab environment, bypassed its systems to gain access to the open internet and hacked a different company’s internal system.

“[T]here is a real risk that capability development rapidly accelerates beyond our ability to understand or control the resulting systems,” the signees said. “To realize AI’s potential, industry, government, and society at large may need the option to buy time to address emerging risks, develop security measures, and strengthen oversight.” [...] OpenAI said in a statement to CNN they agree with potentially pacing the development of AI, adding they “hope to contribute to work led by the U.S. government, alongside other labs” on the topic.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman suggested it may be time to slow down AI development in a podcast interview Tuesday. The OpenAI models that broke out of their test environment are fueling “long term questions” about how AI companies should address this new rate of progress.

“[W]e may have to pace the rate of AI development to give ourselves enough time for society to harden around these new capability levels,” Altman said.

Anthropic said in a statement they are “glad to see broad agreement” on the need to potentially slow AI development “so society can prepare.” [...] See all topics

results.input: Viết giúp mình một hàm Python tính Fibonacci bằng recursion.

result.actual_text:
Chắc chắn rồi! Đây là hàm tính Fibonacci bằng recursion trong Python:

```python
def fibonacci(n):
    """Tính số Fibonacci thứ n bằng recursion."""
    if n < 0:
        raise ValueError("n phải là số nguyên không âm")
    if n == 0:
        return 0
    if n == 1:
        return 1
    return fibonacci(n - 1) + fibonacci(n - 2)


# Ví dụ sử dụng
if __name__ == "__main__":
    for i in range(10):
        print(f"F({i}) = {fibonacci(i)}")
```

**Kết quả:**
```
F(0) = 0
F(1) = 1
F(2) = 1
F(3) = 2
F(4) = 3
F(5) = 5
F(6) = 8
F(7) = 13
F(8) = 21
F(9) = 34
```

**Giải thích:**
- **Case cơ sở (base case):** `F(0) = 0` và `F(1) = 1` — đây là điều kiện dừng để recursion không chạy vô hạn.
- **Case đệ quy (recursive case):** `F(n) = F(n-1) + F(n-2)` — hàm gọi lại chính nó hai lần với `n-1` và `n-2`.

**⚠️ Lưu ý:** Cách này có độ phức tạp thời gian **O(2ⁿ)** vì tính lại nhiều giá trị trùng lặp. Với `n` lớn sẽ rất chậm. Nếu cần hiệu suất tốt hơn, bạn có thể dùng **memoization** (bộ nhớ đệm):

```python
from functools import lru_cache

@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def fibonacci_memo(n):
    if n < 0:
        raise ValueError("n phải là số nguyên không âm")
    if n <= 1:
        return n
    return fibonacci_memo(n - 1) + fibonacci_memo(n - 2)
```

Phiên bản `@lru_cache` sẽ lưu kết quả mỗi lần tính, giảm độ phức tạp xuống **O(n)** — nhanh hơn rất nhiều cho `n` lớn.

In state-of-the-art robotics applications, generative AI systems called vision-language-action (VLA) models act as the brain of a robot, planning its next moves and executing those actions.

We look forward to expanding our work into the latest world action models, so it has even stronger capabilities as we keep pushing to make physical AI faster,” says Song Han, an associate professor in the MIT Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (EECS), member of the Research Laboratory of Electronics, and lead author of a paperon this method. [...] This new method doubled the speed of robots performing activities like pick-and-place tasks, while significantly reducing lag time between motions. It also boosted the performance of robotic arms in highly dynamic activities, such as playing table tennis and Whack-a-Mole.

items.title: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to unde
items.summary: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to understand what you're trying to achieve, but you're too lazy to type them. In these cases I like to lean back, switch to /voice and just ramble for like 10 minutes, total mess, anything goes, full stream of consciousness. Sometimes I declare it up top, something like "switching to speech recognition sorry for any typos...". Sometimes I turn it into a small interview of a few turns. But I find that the LLMs are somehow very good at reconstructing long incoherent rambles and often their echo of your own tangle of thoughts comes out quite a bit cleaner than what you started with. The result is that you improve the mind meld and have to correct things less from that point on.
